document.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Fix DP/EP dynamic per-tensor FP8 scales
document.body:
## Purpose

Fix incorrect dynamic per-tensor FP8 activation scaling in the naive DP/EP all-gather/reduce-scatter path.

Before this change, each rank quantized its local activation independently:

```text
X_r [M_r, K] BF16
  -> Q_r [M_r, K] FP8 + s_r [1]
  -> all-gather
```

The gathered activation therefore contained row segments encoded with different scales, while the expert kernel accepts one per-tensor scale for the complete gathered tensor.

This caused two failure modes:

- Equal token counts: multiple rank-local scales were gathered, but the expert kernel consumed only one scalar.
- Unequal token counts: all-gatherv applied token-row sizes to a local scale tensor containing only one element and failed before expert execution.

This PR delays quantization for dynamic per-tensor FP8 W8A8 until after dispatch:

```text
X_r [M_r, K] BF16
  -> all-gather
X_global [sum(M_r), K] BF16
  -> dynamic per-tensor FP8 quantization
Q_global [sum(M_r), K] FP8 + s_global [1]
```

All rows in `Q_global` are now encoded using the same scalar consumed by the expert kernel. The modular and monolithic naive DP/EP paths share the same policy and quantization helper.

The change is restricted to:

- FP8 W8A8;
- dynamic activation scaling (`a1_scale is None`);
- per-tensor activation quantization;
- callers that have not already deferred input quantization.

Static FP8, per-token/block FP8, non-FP8 paths, and existing caller-deferred paths keep their previous behavior.

The affected path now communicates BF16 activations instead of FP8 activations before quantizing the gathered tensor. This is the correctness trade-off required to compute one valid tensor-wide scale.

## Test Plan

Run the committed policy and two-GPU DP/EP regression tests:

```bash
pytest -q tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py \
  -k 'test_should_quantize_after_dispatch or test_allgather_reducescatter_fp8_dynamic_per_tensor_scale'
```

The committed suite contains five policy cases and two modular-path
distributed cases. The distributed test covers:

```text
equal token counts:   [2, 2]
unequal token counts: [2, 3]
```

For each layout, the test constructs an independent global-FP8 oracle and verifies:

- the returned activation scale contains exactly one scalar;
- the returned scale exactly matches the global scale (`atol=0`, `rtol=0`);
- every returned FP8 activation byte exactly matches the oracle (`torch.equal`).

The policy test additionally verifies that post-dispatch quantization is selected only for dynamic per-tensor FP8, and not for:

- an existing caller-deferred path;
- static FP8;
- per-token/block FP8;
- non-FP8 quantization.

For additional validation, temporarily parameterize the same distributed test
over both naive DP/EP implementations:

```text
prepare implementation: modular, monolithic
rank token counts:       [2, 2], [2, 3]
```

Run formatting and lint checks on the two changed files:

```bash
pre-commit run ruff-check --files \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/naive_dp_ep.py

pre-commit run ruff-format --files \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_layer.py \
  vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/prepare_finalize/naive_dp_ep.py
```

## Test Result

Tested with two NVIDIA B200 GPUs. All results below are from executed tests,
not inferred outcomes.

### Committed regression suite after the fix

```text
test_allgather_reducescatter_fp8_dynamic_per_tensor_scale[False] PASSED
test_allgather_reducescatter_fp8_dynamic_per_tensor_scale[True]  PASSED

dynamic per-tensor FP8, defer=False -> PASSED (post-dispatch=True)
dynamic per-tensor FP8, defer=True  -> PASSED (post-dispatch=False)
static per-tensor FP8               -> PASSED (post-dispatch=False)
per-token/block FP8                 -> PASSED (post-dispatch=False)
non-FP8                             -> PASSED (post-dispatch=False)

7 passed in 34.91s
```

### Additional modular and monolithic validation after the fix

The distributed regression was temporarily parameterized over both prepare
implementations without changing its input or oracle assertions. This
validation-only parameterization is not part of the PR commit.

```text
modular,    equal [2, 2]   PASSED
monolithic, equal [2, 2]   PASSED
modular,    uneven [2, 3]  PASSED
monolithic, uneven [2, 3]  PASSED

9 passed, 491 deselected, 15 warnings in 71.18s
```

The nine passing cases consist of the four distributed cases above and the
five committed policy cases.

### Baseline implementation

Only `naive_dp_ep.py` was replaced with its parent-commit version while the
same four-case validation test and environment were retained:

```text
modular,    equal [2, 2]   FAILED: a1q_scale.numel() != 1
monolithic, equal [2, 2]   FAILED: a1q_scale.numel() != 1
modular,    uneven [2, 3]  FAILED: AssertionError: 1 != 2 / 1 != 3
monolithic, uneven [2, 3]  FAILED: AssertionError: 1 != 2 / 1 != 3

4 failed, 496 deselected, 15 warnings in 65.15s
```

The equal-token failures show that the gathered scale contains multiple
rank-local values instead of the one scalar required by the per-tensor expert
kernel. The uneven-token failures occur earlier because all-gatherv applies
token row sizes `[2, 3]` to each local scale tensor of size `[1]`.

### Formatting and lint

```text
ruff check   Passed
ruff format  Passed
```
